summary.text: Suhas Subramanyam is the Democratic incumbent seeking a second term representing Virginia's 10th District. A lawyer who worked in the Obama White House on technology policy, he served in the Virginia House of Delegates and State Senate before winning the congressional seat in 2024. He serves on the House Oversight, Science, Space, and Technology, and Ethics committees.

paragraphs.text: Subramanyam was born on September 26, 1986, in Houston, Texas, to physician parents who emigrated from India.
He earned a B.A. in philosophy from Tulane University in 2008 and a J.D. from Northwestern University's Pritzker School of Law in 2013.
He began his career as a legislative aide, including for U.S. Rep. Suzanne Kosmas of Florida, and clerked for the U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee while in law school.

Subramanyam worked as an attorney and as a policy advisor and special assistant for technology policy in the Obama White House, and he also worked in the private sector with several tech startups and started his own business.
He won the 87th District seat in the Virginia House of Delegates in 2019 and served until 2024; he co-founded a bipartisan caucus and passed bills on K-12 education, taxes and gun safety.

After defeating Ibraheem Samirah in the Democratic primary, he won the Virginia State Senate's 32nd District seat in 2023, taking office in January 2024; his official biography says he passed legislation lowering tolls, utility bills and prescription-drug costs across his time in the legislature.
Subramanyam won Virginia's 10th Congressional District in the November 2024 general election, succeeding Rep. Jennifer Wexton, and took office in January 2025.

In the House he serves on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, where he is ranking member of the Military and Foreign Affairs Subcommittee, the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and the Committee on Ethics.

According to his official biography, he and his wife, Miranda Peña Subramanyam, live with their two daughters in Loudoun County, where he has volunteered as a firefighter and EMT with the Loudoun Medical Reserve Corps.
